title: Turn each carton's label toward a fixed scanner as the cartons ride a moving line
instruction: Before each carton reaches the scanner gate, turn it on its carrier so that its shipping label faces the scanner on the far side of the line. Leave each carton standing upright on its own carrier, and let go of it before it reaches the gate.
context: On parcel and warehouse lines a fixed scanner reads the barcode on one side of each passing carton; a carton whose label faces elsewhere is a no-read and goes to manual handling, so workers beside the line turn cartons label-out as they go by, without stopping the line or knocking them off. Done by: parcel sorters, warehouse line operators, induction workers.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Conveyor line: a black track bed (12 cm wide along x, 124 cm long along y, 1.5 cm tall) centred at x = 0.34, y = 0, ending 3 cm inside each table edge. Three grey aluminium carrier plates (10 x 10 x 1.5 cm), square to the line, ride 2 mm above the bed, their centres at y = -0.12, -0.34 and -0.56 at the start (22 cm apart). Each carries one closed brown corrugated-cardboard carton (6 x 6 cm footprint, 8 cm tall, 150 g, contents packed tight) standing upright in its middle, sides square to the line. On one side of each carton is a white paper shipping label (5 cm wide, 5 cm tall, centred across the side, its bottom 1.8 cm above the carton's bottom) printed with black barcode bars, and above it an orange paper band (5 cm wide) that covers the top 1.2 cm of that side and folds over the top edge 1.5 cm onto the carton's top. The label faces: carton 1 (leading, at y = -0.12) toward the right (-y, back along the line); carton 2 (y = -0.34) toward the robot (-x); carton 3 (y = -0.56) toward the left (+y, the way the line moves). Scanner gate, fixed to the table at y = 0.50: two dark grey posts (3 x 3 cm, 20 cm tall) centred at x = 0.225 and x = 0.455 (11.5 cm either side of the line's centre), a dark grey crossbar (26 x 3 x 3 cm) across their tops, and a black scanner head (2 cm deep along x, 7 cm along y, 6 cm tall, centred 7.2 cm above the table) on the line-side face of the far post (x = 0.455), with a red window (5 x 2 cm) on its face toward the line. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start in their ready pose, grippers open. The line starts with the trial: the carriers speed up from rest to 4 cm/s in 0.5 s and run on at that speed toward the left, so the carriers' centres pass the gate at 15.75 s, 21.25 s and 26.75 s; past the table's left edge the line turns down and drops the carriers and anything on them out of reach.
scoring: Each carton is read once, at the moment its carrier's centre reaches the gate (y = 0.50). It is read if at that moment: it stands on its own carrier (its centre within 3 cm of the carrier's centre in each of x and y, its underside within 1 cm of the carrier's top); it is upright (its top within 10 degrees of straight up; lying on a side or upside down fails); both grippers' grasp points (between the fingers) are 8 cm or more from its centre; its label faces within 20 degrees of straight at the scanner (+x, seen from above); and it has never touched the table (its lowest corner within 1 cm of the table top) during the trial. Score: one third per carton read (0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1). The trial ends with 1.0 once all three have been read (held 1 s). No carton starts readable (each label is 90 or 180 degrees off), so doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Stop the line, put the carriers back at their starting positions with a carton in the middle of each, labels facing as in the setup, and start the line with the trial. Catch cartons that run off the end of the line. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: The carriers follow their path exactly, like a stiff servo-driven pallet conveyor: the arms can't push or stop them. They float 2 mm above the bed and past the table's edge move straight down. Each carton is one rigid box of even mass; label, barcode and orange band are visual only. Friction 0.9/0.8; at under 0.15 m/s² the line doesn't slide them. The scanner isn't optical: the score applies its read rule (label within 20° of facing it) geometrically at the gate.
